Exiting a root prompt from a group can keep internal positions and jump it to the wrong place. Release outside the tab bar can leave live preview state behind because cleanup did not finalize the drag.

In shared outline lists, the first upward move can go the wrong way because boundary math uses row height instead of real row pitch. If a hidden section changes scroller height during drag, the whole list reflows and the chosen boundary becomes unstable. A drag can also lose its cursor anchor or post-drop scroll lease when underfill and spacer geometry are mismeasured.

A grouped item may move one root step and then stop being able to enter nested rows, because the UI shows one boundary while the drag state commits another.
